question: What do official Gemini CLI sources establish about MCP discovery, permissions, trust, timeouts, environment sanitization, and resource reads, and what remains unknown about external effects?
scope: public first-party Google Gemini CLI sources only; read-only research

sources.evidence_window: MCP architecture, transports, settings, trust, timeout, environment sanitization, resources
sources.cannot_prove: third-party server safety, external commit, exactly-once, post-timeout status
freshness, completeness, authorization correctness, business effect
successful execution, durable secret safety, effect confirmation

claims.claim: Official docs describe MCP discovery, registration, execution, confirmation logic, and timeout handling.

sources.support: MCP architecture, discovery/execution layers, transports, confirmation logic, and timeout handling.

claims.caveat: Documented behavior is not proof of production external-effect completion.

claims.claim: allowed/excluded and includeTools/excludeTools provide documented server/tool filtering; excludeTools wins over includeTools.

sources.support: Global allowed/excluded and per-server includeTools/excludeTools configuration sections.

claims.caveat: Filtering policy does not prove that an allowed tool is safe.

claims.claim: trust=true bypasses all tool-call confirmations for the server, default false.

sources.support: Server configuration property trust and its documented confirmation behavior.

claims.caveat: Bypassing confirmation is not a safety or correctness attestation.

claims.claim: The documented MCP request timeout default is 600000 ms; timeout does not establish whether a remote side effect happened.

sources.support: Configuration property timeout documents a 10-minute default; the page does not define external commit semantics after timeout.

claims.caveat: Post-timeout remote state remains unknown without target read-back.

claims.claim: Sensitive inherited environment variables are redacted by default; explicitly configured env variables are trusted and exempt from automatic redaction.

sources.support: Environment expansion and security/environment sanitization sections.

claims.caveat: Explicit sharing still exposes the variable to the configured MCP process.

claims.claim: Exactly-once, cancellation-after-timeout, remote durability, complete audit coverage, and external business commit remain unknown from these docs.

sources.support: The cited documentation describes client integration and configuration but does not specify these external-effect guarantees.
Resource interaction reference does not establish freshness, completeness, or business-effect guarantees.

claims.caveat: Do not infer failure or absence from timeout/disconnect alone; reconcile against the authoritative target.

limitations: No real MCP server or credential was used
No production or remote service was accessed
Official documentation is evidence of documented behavior, not proof of every implementation/runtime outcome
